Signal quality

What can this recording tell us?

Useful for: locating motion bursts, reviewing swing rhythm, and developing a candidate counter.

Still unverified: smash count, shuttle contact, actual maximum rotation, racket speed, and sensor noise floor.

Clipped peaks cannot be restored by filtering. Record a stationary segment and labeled swings or synchronized video to validate the next iteration.

Method, limitations & badminton references

Signals use seconds relative to the first row. The detector linearly interpolates magnitude onto a 100 Hz grid, then applies a Gaussian filter (σ20 ms), local peak prominence and minimum separation. It checks gyro magnitude within ±0.15 s. Interpolation bridges pauses only for exploratory detection; it cannot recover missing peaks. Red bands indicate observed runs near ±16 g or ±1024°/s, assuming this device configuration. They do not label unobserved intervals. No classifier is used.

Continuous sequence numbers only establish continuity of recorded software samples. They cannot prove every hardware update was acquired. The repository documents approximately 112.1 Hz, which should be checked against the device configuration if row timing differs. Reported clipping percentages are percentages of rows, not time.

References: Wrist IMU classification · BadminSense smartwatch dataset · Racket IMU segmentation & classification · Wearable motion detection. Placement, units and sample rates must be matched before transferring models; review each repository’s license.
